title: Match bond length and strength
hints: Think of more shared electron density between the nuclei.
Compare the result with each choice and check its sign, units, or underlying rule.
solution: Increasing order increases typical bond strength and decreases typical length in this same-element series.
statement:
Which qualitative trend is expected for C–C, C=C and C≡C in comparable compounds?

[_]{a}

choices: Increasing order usually shortens and strengthens the bond.
Increasing order lengthens and weakens the bond.
Increasing order shortens and weakens the bond.
Increasing order lengthens and strengthens the bond.
explanations: Both comparisons apply to similar C–C bonds.
Higher order usually also strengthens it.
The expected length trend is reversed.
